rationale: Reviewed 7404845f401f4839d4ddec0ce3969d65ac9270fe, the full current BRIEF, my round-4 verdict, consolidated-round-4.md, the round-5 diff, the resulting spec, ADR-0045 and its back-pointers, and relevant production code. Both of my round-4 asks are ADDRESSED. Fresh scratch-only probes reproduced all six baseline claims. Two NEW_ISSUEs prevent approval: F2 orders independent panel registrations by counters that are local to each panel, allowing a genuinely later unlanded review to pass; and the new plan-read laziness rule forbids the read required to distinguish N1 from N4 in detached-only ready sets. These are specification corrections before planning, not requests to implement the feature at this gate. Spec validation exits 0 with one lifecycle-binding warning. Production behavior and explicitly labeled emulations of the future normative predicates are distinguished in the evidence. The source worktree was treated read-only; the independent clone, fake bd, real-git fixtures, embedded bd database, build/cache files, probes and logs are under the assigned scratch directory. GitHub API access failed.
concrete_changes_required: Correct R4.2 F2 (spec.md:404-409), its ADR-0041 amendment contract and AC-11: panel.json round is a per-panel-directory counter, not a bead-global chronology. A lower round in a different registration must not by itself prove that its unlanded review predates an anchor. Define an ordering that is actually justified by the available provenance, or fail closed when the registrations are incomparable; this can be done without implementing the deferred panel substrate. Add acceptance and read-back regressions in which an old slug reaches round 5 on landed A, a later new slug starts at its normal round 1 on unlanded B, both registrations are visible in the scanned roots, and bead/X is absent or reset to A. Reattest must refuse without writing, and an existing matching valid audit tuple must not allow automatic read-back. Keep a positive earlier-rebased-round case only where its ordering is established rather than inferred from independent local counters.

Correct the lazy plan-read trigger in R1.1(c) (spec.md:249) so it also reads when a near-miss classification needs the mapping, including plan-form rows with no lineage or another epic resolved by title. Preserve the no-read behavior for a genuinely empty/no-plan-form set and any classifications that can short-circuit independently of mapping. Add a standalone fixture whose entire ready set is one neutral-title, parentless <E>.1: with positional section 1 AND chunk 1 it must be N1, blocking, with the reparent recovery; with the same section but no chunk 1 it must be N4, informational, with no reparent recovery. Both calls have zero rows with lineage E, so the present lazy trigger cannot implement both required outcomes. Test the corresponding title-to-E2 case if it uses the same trigger.

findings.title: Round-4 ask status
findings.detail: G1r4.1 ADDRESSED. R4.2 now requires a VALID audited accepted pair to equal both the current binding and the single independently scanned candidate, and re-runs F1-F5 on reads (spec.md:420-432). AC-11(xii) expressly pins the M1 audit / normal executor M2 rewrite regression, including the multiple-candidate refusal. A fresh probe uses the real ReattestLandedMerge, ensureLandedBinding and MergeMetadata, extends only the audit writer in a labeled emulation of the planned new fields, and verifies that the normal executor preserves the old tuple but that tuple does not equal M2; F1 independently refuses the two candidates. Evidence: audited-tuple-probe.log and repo/internal/executor/g1_round5_audit_probe_test.go. G1r4.2 ADDRESSED. R1.3:306-307 limits the MF-1-only override to N4 with lineage E and gives lineage-none N4 its pre-gate refusal; AC-3 pins no GateReadiness call and byte-identical audit. The current production baseline again returns report=nil and ErrNoEpicLineage for the detached neutral-title shape even with the broad override. Evidence: baseline-probes.log. The two required changes below are NEW_ISSUEs in the round-5 rules.

findings.title: F2 compares panel-local rounds as though they establish chronology across registrations
findings.detail: R4.2 F2:404-409 exempts a non-ancestor review whenever its round is below the highest anchor round. Production panel.Create accepts Round as a caller-supplied value and writes one directory; cmd/mindspec/panel.go:329 defaults each create to round 1. There is no bead-global sequence. A later panel under another slug legitimately starts at 1 after an older panel reached 5. The real-git probe creates a real landing of A, writes old-panel round 5 through the real panel.Create, commits later B on bead/X, writes new-panel round 1 through panel.Create, deletes bead/X, and applies the #239 topology. Real panel.Scan/ForBead sees both registrations. B is not an ancestor of the spec tip. There is exactly one admitted fallback candidate, its effect remains at the tip (real gitutil.RevertShape=false), and no surviving branch contradicts it. An executable transcription of the new F2 returns PASS with highest_anchor_round=5, although B is genuinely later and unlanded. Changing only new-panel round 1 to 6 makes the negative control refuse. Thus the new acceptance contract admits this shape, and a matching genuine earlier audit can remain acceptable after this later review. This is a specification-predicate probe, not a claim that the unimplemented fallback already passes in production. No panel or audit forgery is needed. Evidence: attack-probes.log; repo/internal/lifecycle/g1_round5_attack_probe_test.go. Ancestor transitivity itself is sound: a SHA outside the tip cannot be an ancestor of the reachable second parent. The failure is treating independent round counters as temporal provenance.

findings.title: The lazy plan read cannot classify a ready set containing only detached near-misses
findings.detail: R1.1(c):249 says plan.md is read ONLY when at least one plan-form row has lineage E. R1.2:274-276 nevertheless needs the plan to distinguish N1 (mapped, no lineage) from N4 (unmapped, no lineage), with different diagnostics, recoveries and exit codes. Consider the entire global ready set containing only neutral-title <E>.1 with no parent/dependency: the real resolver gives ErrNoEpicLineage, so the lazy trigger is false. With a positional section and chunk 1 the required answer is blocking N1 / exit 1 / bd update --parent E. Removing only chunk 1 makes it informational N4 / exit 0 / bd show, with no reparent advice. A reader forbidden to inspect either plan cannot tell those inputs apart. The fresh mapping probe uses the production ParsePlanFrontmatter and extractBeadSectionRaw and obtains those different structural mappings; the classification/exit calculation is explicitly the future spec predicate. The mixed AC-1 fixture conceals the gap because A/G already trigger the read. The same dependency on mapping exists for title-resolved E2 rows (N2b versus N4). Evidence: plan-map-probe.log; repo/internal/validate/readiness/g1_round5_baseline_probe_test.go. The shared positional-section AND work_chunks mapping itself agrees with MF-1; its read trigger is the problem.

findings.title: Six baseline claims reproduced at the reviewed commit
findings.detail: Fresh fake bd on PATH: global QueryReady returns detached probe-epic.1, while the edge-only --parent query used by BuildReadySet returns raw=0, filtered=0 and notice="". A successful stderr notice "Showing 100 of 106 ready issues..." is discarded and QueryReady returns 100 rows with nil error. Fresh real git: the first-parent control identifies the landing; after sibling integration that same merge remains reachable, but FindLandedMerge returns ErrLandedMergeNoCandidate. Real panel.json files a-stale and z-match produce the lexically first stale-SHA contradiction despite an exact surviving tip; removing a-stale restores identification. MF-2 R9(a) against identical spec text fails as dangling, and AC9 harvests zero claims. Fresh real bd 1.1.0 (8e4e59d39), in a new embedded scratch database: ready --metadata-field spec_id=129-probe -n 0 returns both the detached dotted child and metadata-only task; ready --parent still returns the detached child by prefix; ready -n 1 returns one of four rows and emits the cap notice at exit 0. This supports the corrected Background A: edge-only parent dropping is a fake-bd version variant, not bd 1.1.0 behavior. The historical live-tracker count 106 was not re-measured. Evidence: baseline-probes.log, bd-real-probes.json, bd-probes.log, bd-ids.json and the three baseline probe files in the scratch clone.
